judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause runs two unrelated ideas together — assignment not binding without consent, and cover continuing for the insured's legal representative for the unexpired term — with words plainly missing, so its meaning is not recoverable from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the policy addresses assignment or death of the insured, so the defect is intrinsic rather than relational.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Excess over any other valid and collectible insurance available to the insured, whether or not described in the Schedule' with a proviso for contribution is a notoriously contested formula, and 'collectible' and 'contributing' are undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be reconciled with Definition d (c034), which folds 'any other underlying insurance collectible' into the retained limit, and with the Overlap Endorsement (c106) dealing with inter-insurer disputes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The apportionment waterfall is detailed and orderly; the drafting is mechanical rather than open-textured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement (c071) adds a made-whole rule that reverses the priority in the first tier, so the two must be read together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional no-waiver/endorsement-only clause stated in one sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Wisconsin Amendatory Endorsement's CHANGES provision (c072) makes an agent's knowledge the company's knowledge and forbids voiding the policy on that ground, which directly contradicts this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scan has lost words from the insured-cancellation sentence, and the 'thirty (20) days' figure is internally inconsistent on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Cancellation - Wisconsin endorsement (c063-c069) substitutes 10- and 60-day regimes and Endorsement No. 3 (c092) requires 60 days, so three different notice periods coexist.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The warranty is stated as an obligation and then defused by a deeming provision ('shall apply in the same manner as it would have applied had such policies been so maintained'), which is hard to square within the same paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Loss Payable (c048), Definition d (c034) and the Wisconsin Declarations endorsement (c073) on promissory warranties, the consequence of a lapse in underlying cover is not consistently stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except insofar as coverage is available to the insured in the underlying insurance listed' is incomplete ('listed' where?) and 'available' could mean scheduled, in force, or actually responsive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its follow-form carve-back depends on the Item 7 schedule and on the CGL underlying policy, which is not reproduced, so the exclusion's operative width can only be settled by reference to other documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It cross-refers to the 'self insured retention listed in Item 7 of the Declarations' when the SIR is stated in Item 4 and Item 7 is the schedule of underlying insurance — a mechanical error going to the trigger of the carve-back.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It guts the Personal Injury definition (c035) for a hospital risk and its wrong cross-reference cannot be reconciled with the Declarations, which place the SIR in Item 4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Initiated, alleged or caused to be brought about by a Named Insured against any other Named Insured' is broad and 'caused to be brought about' has no clear boundary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With more than a dozen Named Insureds added by c085, c115, c117 and c120, the exclusion may swallow claims the additional-insured endorsements appear to cover.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The conditional opening 'if this policy applies to professional liability' leaves the reader to determine whether the condition is ever satisfied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Professional Services Excluded endorsement (c082) removes professional health care services, while the Aggregate Limits Endorsement (c084) and the Contingent Excess endorsement (c102) assume some professional cover exists, so whether this carve-out ever operates is genuinely unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence disapplying the endorsement to intrafamily automobile liability; concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the omnibus auto clause (c022) and the scheduled Sentry auto policy without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It identifies the form it modifies as 'UML-002 (4/91)' whereas the policy form is UML 002 (1/91), a citation slip, but the substitution itself is purely formal.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces the attestation clause at the foot of the base form; the mismatch in form date is the only friction with the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence merges two alternative methods (surrender, or mailing written notice) without the disjunctive, so it reads as requiring both and omits any effective-date default.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Condition 12 (c055) states the insured's cancellation right differently, and Item 6 of the Declarations imposes a short-rate minimum premium on insured cancellation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare lead-in with no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It introduces (a)-(e) below and conflicts with nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two conditions (in force less than 60 days and not a renewal) are stated cumulatively and clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations show this policy 'Renews UML-95-4104-00-OH', so this paragraph appears inapplicable, and Endorsement No. 3 (c092) mandates 60 days' notice in any event.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Cancellation for non-payment on 10 days' notice is a definite rule tied to a definite default.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 3 (c092) requires 60 days' written notice 'in the event of cancellation or non-renewal' without carving out non-payment, and the Pay Plan (c098) supplies the due dates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The three enumerated grounds are specific, though 'substantial change in the risk assumed' and 'substantial breaches' are matters of degree.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 10-day notice conflicts with Condition 12's thirty days (c055) and with Endorsement No. 3's sixty days (c092).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening words 'if in addition to the right of the Company to cancel as provided for in paragraph (b) and (c) above and provided that if' are ungrammatical and leave the conditions tangled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations fix a one-year term (03/01/1996 to 03/01/1997), so the paragraph is dormant, and Endorsement No. 3 (c092) again overlays a 60-day rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The typo 'a right te to renewal' aside, the guaranteed-renewal mechanism and 60-day notice are stated with precision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aligns with Endorsement No. 3's 60-day non-renewal notice (c092) but creates a renewal entitlement not reflected anywhere else in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence — 'Any person or organization or the legal representative thereof shall be entitled to recover under this policy to the extent of the insurance afforded' — is startlingly broad and sits against a strict compliance condition precedent in the sentence before it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deletes and replaces Condition 6 (c049) and duplicates Condition 7 (c050), and its open recovery right is hard to reconcile with the Loss Payable condition (c048).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Fully compensated for damages' is a made-whole formula whose measure is not spelled out but is familiar in Wisconsin law.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reverses the first tier of the apportionment waterfall in Condition 10 (c053), which is added rather than deleted, so the two orderings must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear statutory-style rule imputing agent knowledge to the company; the citation to 'Section 637.09(1)' looks like a slip for 631.09 but nothing operative turns on it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely contradicts Condition 11 (c054), which says notice to or knowledge of any agent shall not effect a waiver or change.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The misrepresentation and warranty rules are carefully staged with express materiality and causation tests.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts across Condition 13's warranty of maintenance of underlying insurance (c056) and Condition 3's notice duties (c046) by limiting the consequences of breach.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any insured subject of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act' is garbled (subject to? subject of?) and 'arising out of' extends the exclusion indefinitely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision grants fiduciary or benefit-plan cover, so the exclusion stands alone.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excluding property merely 'used by any Insured' and property 'as to which any insured ... are for any purpose exercising physical control' is extremely broad, and 'for any purpose' has no discernible limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The base-form exclusion (c024) covers the same ground but only 'to the extent the insured is under contract to provide insurance', so the endorsement and the policy exclusion are of different width without saying which governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence excluding directors and officers for 'wrongful acts', a term defined immediately below.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the carve-out in c078 and with the insured definition (c021), which brings executive officers and directors in as insureds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing words 'solely by reason of their being directors or officers of the company' use 'the company', which throughout this policy means the insurer, not the insured entity — a defined-term slip that changes the scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy's own usage of 'the company' for Ohio Hospital Insurance Company (Conditions 1-13) is what makes the phrase incoherent here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out lists 'personal injury, bodily injury, property damage, hospital professional liability or advertisers liability', mixing defined and undefined terms ('bodily injury', 'advertisers liability') so its reach is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves 'hospital professional liability' although the Professional Services Excluded endorsement (c082) removes exactly that, and 'advertisers liability' does not match the defined 'Advertising Liability' (c037).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, flat sentence removing discrimination from the personal injury definition; nothing internally ambiguous except the width of 'arising out of'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Definition e(5) (c035) expressly includes racial or religious discrimination within personal injury, so the endorsement and the definition point in opposite directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scanned text has lost the opening words of each sentence, so the exclusion's subject and its 'at any time' timing language are not readable as drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies to 'bodily injury', a term this policy does not define, and overlaps the Total Pollution Exclusion (c094) without either saying which controls.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A defence disclaimer whose text is fragmentary here, but the concept — no duty to defend asbestos suits — is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It withdraws the supplementary-payments defence obligation (c003, c004) for asbestos suits, an intended carve-out rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Professional health care services' is defined only by an inclusive list ('including the furnishing of food, beverages, medications or appliances'), leaving the general term's reach at large for a hospital insured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Aggregate Limits Endorsement (c084) aggregates 'any professional liability hazard' and the Contingent Excess endorsement (c100-c104) contemplates professional cover dropping down, so the instrument as a whole is not clear whether professional liability is in or out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A double negative — the exclusion 'does not apply to those entities or individuals that are not subject to the Wisconsin Patients Compensation Fund' — which is easy to read either way and turns on an undefined statutory status.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with the Contingent Excess endorsement (c102-c104) and the Professional Liability Limits endorsement (c121), which use the same Fund status test for different purposes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The added tail 'or any professional liability hazard' introduces an undefined hazard category alongside the defined products and completed operations hazards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces Insuring Agreement III (c013), assumes professional liability cover that c082 excludes, and rests on declared limits that Endorsement No. 4 (c109) purports to change to $20M/$20M.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of named entities with one qualification ('no automatic coverage for entities newly acquired by any of them'); concrete, though 'newly acquired' is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against the Named Insured definition (c020), which automatically embraces organisations under the named insured's control, and is added to by Endorsements Nos. 6 and 8 (c115, c120).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short deeming rule for cancellation notice; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements Condition 12's first-named-insured provision (c055) but sits alongside three different notice periods (c055, c066-c067, c092).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure attachment boilerplate with no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with every other endorsement's identical attachment language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Only with respect to their interest in the operations of the Named Insured' is a vague limitation, and the schedule pairs each entity with an 'insurable interest' such as 'as their interest may appear'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates 'additional insureds' where the policy elsewhere speaks of 'named insureds' (c085) and defines 'insured' in Definition b (c021, c031), leaving the category's status uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the identical wording in the other General Amendatory Endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The limitation 'but only as respects Med-Health Financial Services' is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The attached form itself (c099) is drafted to apply to 'the Insured' generally, so the two must be read together to know how far the exclusion reaches.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No tension with anything else.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence, unqualified 60-day notice requirement; on its own it is perfectly definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot be squared with Condition 12's thirty days (c055) or with the Wisconsin cancellation endorsement's ten days for non-payment and mid-term cancellation (c066, c067).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It identifies the replaced exclusion only by a paraphrase of its subject matter, so which text is displaced depends on matching descriptions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The base-form pollution exclusion (c028) is worded differently from this description, leaving room to argue the 'sudden and accidental' carve-back survives.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Actual, alleged or threatened discharge ... of pollutants' with a 'hostile fire' carve-back is heavily litigated wording, and the exclusion is cast in terms of 'bodily injury', which this policy does not define.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy insures 'personal injury' as defined in c035, so an exclusion phrased in terms of undefined 'bodily injury' does not mesh with the grant of coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clean-up-cost limb is enumerated and specific, though 'in any way respond to' is a broad catch-all after a list of specific acts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits with the definition of ultimate net loss (c033), which is confined to damages, so the two point the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant or contaminant' is the archetypal over-broad definition — on its face it captures ordinary hospital substances — and 'including' leaves the list non-exhaustive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Applied literally it would swallow much of the coverage granted by Insuring Agreement I (c002) for a hospital risk, which is the classic whole-instrument argument against it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Past due if not received by the specified due dates' is a plain rule tied to a table.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The consequence of non-payment is set by the Wisconsin cancellation endorsement (c066) and Endorsement No. 3's 60-day notice (c092), which do not agree with each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Errors or omissions, malpractice or mistake of a professional nature ... in the conduct of the insured's business activities as a collection agency' is specific and self-limiting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 2 (c090) restricts this form to Med-Health Financial Services, so read alone the form is broader than the policy intends.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion is anchored to a statutory definition (Wis. Stat. s.655.001), which makes it determinate as drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be read with the Professional Services Excluded endorsement (c082), the professional liability aggregate in c084 and the contingency drop-down in c102, which together leave the professional cover position genuinely muddled.
